content: The test image shows a tomato leaf with a mottled/mosaic pattern — irregular light and dark green areas, no distinct necrotic spots, no yellowing, leaf shape relatively intact. Top candidates: Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Mosaic_Virus, Leaf_Mold.

Now distinguishing between Tomato_Mosaic_Virus and Mosaic_Virus — both look similar but ToMV reference shows slightly darker veins with mottled green on intact leaves. The TYLCV reference shows more dramatic curling/cupping. Spider_Mites showed more bronze stippling on oval leaves.

Verticillium_Wilt shows severe yellowing/browning/necrosis — clearly not the test image. Septoria shows distinct small dark spots with halos — also not matching.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: intact oval/ovate leaf, subtle diffuse mottling with irregular dark/light green patches, no necrosis, no spots, no yellowing, slight leaf texture irregularity
- Rules out: Verticillium_Wilt (yellowing/necrosis), Septoria (distinct spots), Bacterial_Spot, Late_Blight, Early_Blight (all need lesions), Powdery_Mildew (white coating), TYLCV (strong curling/yellowing), Spider_Mites (bronzing/stippling)
- Best match: **Tomato_Mosaic_Virus** — reference images show mottled green/dark-green on leaves with irregular lighter patches, wrinkled texture, and no distinct lesions. Very close competitor is Mosaic_Virus, but ToMV reference showed the purer green-on-green mottling without yellow streaking that better matches the test.
